explanation: In the United Kingdom, cheek kissing is not a standard greeting in most social gatherings; it is typically reserved for close friends, family, or very informal settings. A handshake or a simple verbal greeting is far more common, especially among acquaintances or in professional contexts. Attempting a cheek kiss with a new acquaintance may be perceived as overly familiar or intrusive.
local_tip: When in doubt, offer a firm handshake or a friendly nod and say 'Hello' or 'Nice to meet you' to avoid awkwardness.
regional_note: In London and among younger, more cosmopolitan crowds, a single cheek kiss (right cheek to right cheek) is occasionally used among friends, but it remains less common than in continental Europe.

also_check.note: La bise (two to four cheek kisses) is a standard greeting among friends and acquaintances, varying by region.
Physical contact like kissing is avoided; bowing is the traditional and expected greeting.
One or two cheek kisses are common even among new acquaintances, especially in social settings.
